hints: Separate the differential equation and decompose the rational function before integrating.
Write $dt=dx/[x^2(1+2x)]$ and use $A/x+B/x^2+C/(1+2x)$ for the partial fractions.
Clear denominators to find the three constants, then integrate each term, retaining the logarithms and $-1/x$ term.
Apply $t=0$ when $x=1$, and combine the logarithms into the requested expression in $x$.
walkthrough:
Separate variables in the differential equation $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = x^2(1 + 2x)$:
$$\dfrac{1}{x^2(1 + 2x)}\,\mathrm{d}x = \mathrm{d}t$$

Set up the partial fraction decomposition for repeated linear factor $x^2$ and linear factor $(1 + 2x)$:
$$\dfrac{1}{x^2(1 + 2x)} = \dfrac{A}{x} + \dfrac{B}{x^2} + \dfrac{C}{1 + 2x}$$

Multiply both sides by $x^2(1 + 2x)$ to form the identity:
$$1 = Ax(1 + 2x) + B(1 + 2x) + Cx^2$$

Determine $B$ by substituting $x = 0$:
$$1 = A(0) + B(1 + 0) + C(0) \implies B = 1$$

Determine $C$ by substituting $x = -\dfrac{1}{2}$:
$$1 = A(0) + B(0) + C\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{4}C \implies C = 4$$

Determine $A$ by comparing coefficients of $x^2$:
$$0 = 2A + C \implies 2A + 4 = 0 \implies 2A = -4 \implies A = -2$$
So the partial fractions are:
$$\dfrac{1}{x^2(1 + 2x)} = -\dfrac{2}{x} + \dfrac{1}{x^2} + \dfrac{4}{1 + 2x}$$

Integrate both sides:
$$\int \left(-\dfrac{2}{x} + x^{-2} + \dfrac{4}{1 + 2x}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x = \int 1\,\mathrm{d}t$$
$$-2\ln x - \dfrac{1}{x} + 2\ln(1 + 2x) = t + c$$

Use the initial condition $x = 1$ when $t = 0$ to find the constant of integration $c$:
$$-2\ln(1) - \dfrac{1}{1} + 2\ln(1 + 2(1)) = 0 + c$$
$$0 - 1 + 2\ln 3 = c \implies c = 2\ln 3 - 1$$

Substitute $c = 2\ln 3 - 1$ back into the integrated equation:
$$-2\ln x - \dfrac{1}{x} + 2\ln(1 + 2x) = t + 2\ln 3 - 1$$

Isolate $t$ and combine the logarithmic terms:
$$t = -\dfrac{1}{x} + 1 + 2\ln(1 + 2x) - 2\ln x - 2\ln 3$$
$$t = -\dfrac{1}{x} + 1 + 2[\ln(1 + 2x) - \ln(3x)]$$
$$t = -\dfrac{1}{x} + 2\ln\left(\dfrac{1 + 2x}{3x}\right) + 1$$
